_notes: Ranges keyed by classification, not by individual offense. Offense nodes point here via their 'classification' + 'derived' flags.
nonViolentFelony tables apply when isVFO=false (routes to Article 70.00 / 70.06 / 70.10).

violentFelony tables apply when isVFO=true (routes to 70.02 / 70.04 / 70.08) -- now populated. SUNSET WARNING: PL 70.02(2)(a) and 70.04(2) determinate provisions are repealed September 1, 2027 and revert to indeterminate. Tables below reflect pre-sunset (current) law.
If an offense has a statute-specific sentencing carve-out (rare, e.g. certain weapon offenses), override at the offense level, not here.

offenseOverrides._ref: PL 70.00(3)(a) — offense-specific sentencing for Class A-I felonies
offenseOverrides._note: Overrides the standard Class A-I indeterminate (15-25yr min to life) for offenses with statutory minimum carve-outs. Applied after modifier bumps but before disposition computation.

125.27._ref: PL 70.00(3)(a)(i)(A) — murder in the first degree: min 20-25yr

1._ref: PL 70.00(3)(a)(i)(B) — subd 1: MUST be life without parole

2._ref: PL 70.00(3)(a)(i)(B) — subd 2: MAY be life without parole; otherwise standard A-I 15-25yr

125.26._ref: PL 70.00(3)(a)(i)(B) — aggravated murder: subd 1 LWOP mandatory, subd 2 LWOP optional

130.95._ref: PL 70.00(3)(a)(ii) — predatory sexual assault: min 10-25yr (vs standard A-II 3-8.33yr)

130.96._ref: PL 70.00(3)(a)(ii) — predatory sexual assault against a child: min 10-25yr (vs standard A-II 3-8.33yr)

120.11._ref: PL 70.02(3)(a)(i) — aggravated assault upon a police officer/peace officer: B 10-30yr (vs standard 5-25)

125.11._ref: PL 70.02(3)(b)(iii) — aggravated criminally negligent homicide: C 3.5-20yr (vs standard 3.5-15)

265.19._ref: PL 70.02(3)(b)(iv) — aggravated criminal possession of a weapon: C 5-15yr (vs standard 3.5-15)

120.18._ref: PL 70.02(3)(c)(i) — menacing a police officer/peace officer: D 2-8yr (vs standard 2-7)

265.02._ref: PL 70.02(3)(c)(ii) — criminal possession of a weapon 3rd subd 10: D 3.5-7yr (vs standard 2-7)

125.25._note: Murder 2nd subd 5 (cop-killer provision) gets life without parole per 70.00(3)(a)(i)(B). Not yet implemented — requires subdivision-level override modeling. Other subdivisions use standard A-I sentencing.

drugFelony._ref: PL 70.70 (non-A) / 70.71 (A) — felony drug offender sentencing. Applies to Article 220 and 222 felonies. VFO drug offenses still sentenced per 70.02/70.04/70.08 per 70.70(4).

sexOffenseFelony._ref: PL 70.80 — felony sex offense sentencing. Applies to Article 130 felonies, 230.05/06/11/12/13, 255.26/27, and sexually motivated felonies. All get determinate sentences with sex-offense-specific PRS per 70.45(2-a).

predicateNonViolent_70_80_5b._ref: PL 70.80(5)(b) — predicate felony sex offender, non-violent predicate

predicateViolent_70_80_5c._ref: PL 70.80(5)(c) — predicate felony sex offender, violent predicate

ClassA_II._note: PL 70.00(3)(a)(ii): min 3yr to 8yr 4mo. Predatory sexual assault (130.95/130.96) has 10-25yr min — offense-specific override not yet encoded.

ClassA_I._note: PL 70.00(3)(a)(i): min 15-25yr. Murder 1st (125.27) has 20-25yr min; aggravated murder (125.26) and murder 2nd subd 5 (125.25(5)) get life without parole — offense-specific overrides not yet encoded.

ClassA_II._note: PL 70.06(3)(a)+(4)(a): max life, min 6-12.5yr. Predatory sexual assault (130.95/130.96) has 10-25yr min — offense-specific override.

persistentFelonyOffender_70_10.note: Discretionary. Court MAY sentence as Class A-I. Requires separate judicial finding, not automatic from 2 priors alone.

_notes: Determinate sentences; imposed in whole or half years per PL 70.02(2)(a) / 70.04(2), effective until September 1, 2027.
SUNSET: On September 1, 2027 these sections revert to indeterminate (NB Effective September 1, 2027 clauses). Regenerate this block after legislative update.

Post-release supervision (PRS) is mandatory on all determinate VFO sentences per PL 70.45: ClassB/C 2.5–5 years per 70.45(2)(f); ClassD/E 1.5–3 years per 70.45(2)(e). Default PRS for non-VFO determinate sentences is 5 years flat per 70.45(2); drug (70.70) and sex (70.80) PRS ranges encoded separately when those tracks are implemented.

Class D VFO (70.02(2)(b)): sentence generally follows Class D felony provisions, but MUST be determinate when commitment to DOCCS is required (70.02(3)(c)). Range 2–7 years applies to DOCCS-commitment cases.

70.04 ClassD floor is 5 years (vs 70.02 ClassD floor of 2 years) per 70.04(3)(c). 70.04 ClassE floor is 3 years (vs 70.02 ClassE floor of 1.5 years) per 70.04(3)(d). Confirmed from provided 70.04 text.

70.08 ClassE: no provision in PL 70.08(3) for Class E violent felonies -- 70.08 only covers ClassA_II, ClassB, ClassC, ClassD. A persistent violent felony offender convicted of a ClassE VFO has no 70.08 minimum range. Flag for further legal research.

ClassD._note: Applies when DOCCS commitment required per 70.02(2)(b)/(3)(c); otherwise Class D felony provisions govern

secondFelonyOffenderVFO_70_06_6._ref: PL 70.06(6) — determinate sentence for second felony offender convicted of a VFO. NB Repealed September 1, 2027.

_notes: Indeterminate sentence; maximum term is life imprisonment per PL 70.08(2). Minimum period fixed by court within statutory range per 70.08(3). Source: verbatim from provided PL 70.08 text.
SUNSET: Two versions of 70.08(3) exist. Pre-sunset (current, effective until September 1, 2027) has higher minimums. Post-sunset (effective September 1, 2027) has lower minimums. Both encoded below.
Class E violent felony: NO provision in PL 70.08(3). Statute only covers ClassA_II, ClassB, ClassC, ClassD. Persistent violent felony offender status for ClassE VFO -- gap; flag for legal research.

70.08(3)(a) -- predatory sexual assault (130.95) or predatory sexual assault against a child (130.96)

hateCrimeBump._note: Authoritative home for hate crime sentencing bump logic. Eligibility (isHateCrimeEligible) is determined by HATECRIME_LIST in ny_penal_ontology.json. This block defines what happens to the sentence once eligibility is confirmed and hate_crime_motivated is true.

misdemeanorOrClassCDE.effect: one category higher than base offense classification

ClassB.effect: fixed statutory minimum floors per predicate-offender status
ClassB._note: Not a simple one-class bump — court must apply 485.10(3) minimum floors based on prior record. Requires separate judicial finding.

70.00._ref: 485.10(3)(a) — non-VFO indeterminate, max term at least 6 years

70.02._ref: 485.10(3)(b) — VFO determinate first offender, term at least 8 years

70.04._ref: 485.10(3)(c) — VFO determinate second violent, term at least 12 years

70.05._ref: 485.10(3)(d) — juvenile offender indeterminate, max term at least 4 years

70.06._ref: 485.10(3)(e) — non-VFO predicate, max/determinate term at least 10 years

ClassA_I.effect: flat minimum indeterminate period of at least 20 years
ClassA_I._note: Not a bump at all — applies a floor on the minimum period of an indeterminate sentence. See 485.10(4).

_notes: Dispositions are keyed by classification level (felony/misdemeanor/violation).
Within felony, VFO status determines determinate vs indeterminate — that routing lives in the existing violentFelony/nonViolentFelony tables.
record_statement_required flags when the court must state reasons on record (required for felonies on CD and UD).

definiteSentence.conditions: Court finds imprisonment necessary but indeterminate or determinate would be unduly harsh

intermittentImprisonment.conditions: Not imposing any other sentence of imprisonment; defendant not under other sentence >15 days

probation.conditions: Institutional confinement not necessary; defendant needs guidance/supervision; not inconsistent with ends of justice

conditionalDischarge.conditions: Neither public interest nor ends of justice served by imprisonment; probation not appropriate

unconditionalDischarge.conditions: No proper purpose served by imposing any condition on release

intermittentImprisonment.conditions: Not imposing any other sentence of imprisonment; defendant not under other sentence >15 days

definiteSentence.note: As provided in the law creating the offense; not to exceed 1 year

_notes: Exception paths that can override the primary sentencing disposition.
Each exception has triggering case-fact parameters (from CaseFacts) and a resulting disposition or modification.

armedFelonyOverride.description: If conviction resulted from plea in satisfaction of armed felony indictment, court must impose determinate sentence UNLESS one of three mitigating factors found and court finds alternate sentence consistent with public safety.

domesticViolenceIndeterminate.description: If DV by victim was a factor in causing the offense, court may impose indeterminate sentence instead of determinate.

dwiSplitSentenceVariant.description: For DWI sentences, imprisonment in a split sentence may be up to 1 year instead of the standard 6 months.

_notes: Financial obligations keyed by classification level.
Amounts are statutory defaults; may be updated by legislative amendment.

fine._note: canStandAlone=false is over-restrictive for C/D/E non-drug felonies per 60.01(3)(b) — only Class B and Art 220 drug felonies forbid fine-only. TODO: gate by class.

drugFelonyFine._note: Overrides standard felony fine for Article 220/222 drug felonies.

sexOffenderRegistrationFee._note: Levied on sex offenders required to register under Correction Law art 6-C.

supplementalSexOffenderVictimFee._note: Levied on convictions for Art 130 felonies, incest (255.25/26/27), and Art 263 offenses.

surchargeSummons.description: If jail term not exceeding 60 days, court must issue summons directing defendant to appear within 60 days if surcharge unpaid

_notes: Collateral requirements beyond sentencing and financials.
DNA sample requirement is felony-gated plus enumerated misdemeanors per Exec Law 995-c(3).

dnaSampleRequired.note: Only for enumerated sex/offense misdemeanors — extend when those are added

restitution.description: Court must consider ordering restitution; if not ordered, must state reasons on record. If ordered, 5% collection surcharge added; up to 10% additional surcharge upon filing by collection agency.

juvenileOffender._ref: PL 70.05 — indeterminate sentence for juvenile offender (13-15 yr old charged with felony). Max terms and minimum periods per 70.05(2)/(3).
